reading.body:
CyrusOne Sterling holds 38 megawatts of IT capacity in Virginia, representing 2.4 percent of the state's 1,603 megawatts of disclosed data center power and ranking 13th among Virginia facilities with published figures.

The facility occupies 700,000 square feet, which translates to roughly 950 racks at typical AI training density. This positions it as a meaningful but not dominant contributor to Virginia's known infrastructure base. Virginia itself contains 330 mapped data center facilities, yet nearly all lack published power specifications, making Sterling one of relatively few sites with disclosed capacity data in a state where grid demand from data centers remains largely unmeasured.

The actual significance of this facility for AI scaling cannot be determined from available information. CyrusOne publishes no certifications, power source details, or confirmation whether the 38 megawatts represents current utilization, allocated capacity, or buildout headroom. Grid impact depends equally on what fraction of this power is already committed to existing customers versus available for new AI workloads, and on whether Sterling connects to renewable generation, natural gas, or the regional grid's marginal source. These gaps are typical across the data center industry and reflect how little visibility exists into the power infrastructure supporting AI compute.
